summary: A first-person feature on the farm-to-table movement in autumn 2023, profiling local farmers, a winery, a farmers' market vendor, a chef and an educational farm visited between September 5 and October 30. Each stop highlights a seasonal ingredient (root vegetables, heirloom apples, greens, mushrooms, squash, grapes, tomatoes) and emphasizes sustainability, community and local flavor. It concludes that farmers are the unsung heroes of regional cuisine.
one_line: A tour of local farms, a winery, a market, a restaurant and a school farm showing how autumn 2023 harvests define farm-to-table regional cuisine.
key_facts: On September 5, the author visited Elmwood Acres, a family-run farm operated by Marianne and Tom Foster that supplies seasonal produce to neighboring restaurants and markets and grows organically.
On September 10, Jane and Henry Wilcox of Avalon Farm showed heirloom apples including 'Ashmead's Kernel'; the grove was inherited from Jane's grandparents and apples ripen on the tree.
Avalon Farm's annual apple-tasting event took place on September 15, with crowd favorites of spiced apple chutney with pork loin and an apple-caramel crumble.
On September 22, Varsha Singh of Green Haven Farm, who has a background in agroecology, showed Swiss chard and 'Lacinato' kale and described her regenerative farming as a closed-loop system.
On September 29, Michael Chen at Hidden Spore Homestead showed oyster and shiitake mushrooms grown on logs and substrates using natural materials.
On October 3, Sarah Johnson, owner of Lakeside Growers, presented pumpkins and squashes including a 'Blue Hubbard' squash; the farm's pumpkin patch draws families and chefs.
On October 8, Alex Ramirez, sommelier and vineyard manager at Vineheart Winery, said "Wine is an expression of the land and season."
On October 16, vendor Lucy Torres sold organic heirloom tomatoes at the downtown farmers' market and called markets "a community, a conversation".
On October 23, Chef Ricardo Garcia of TerraBella said his menu is built on local farms; a stand-out October dish was butternut squash ravioli with sage butter.
On October 30, Sandra Meehan, a founder of New Roots Educational Farm, described connecting children to the land through hands-on learning for schools.
The article is dated September 2023 and calls autumn the "harvest season", defining farm-to-table as emphasizing the connection between farms and the food on our plates.
